payload.title: AI Builders Daily · 2026-06-08
payload.summary:
**Claude** gives managed agents memory "dreaming," outcome graders, and multiagent orchestration; **Aaron Levie** says enterprise AI is trapped in a weird loop where model progress keeps outrunning rollout plans.

**Codex** turns up the pressure with a 100-day power-user challenge; builders across X keep hammering the same idea: stop babysitting prompts and start designing loops; tokenmaxxing is giving way to token anxiety and token optimization; routing, retries, and cost-aware orchestration are starting to look like the real moat.

**Claude** 这次把 agent 的底层玩法往前拱了一截，dreaming、结果评分、多 agent 编排一起放出来；**Aaron Levie** 说得很实在，模型进展太快，企业那套 rollout 反而更容易被打断。

**Codex** 又添了一把火，100 天连续挑重度用户放大额度；X 上这波讨论也越来越集中，少纠结 prompt，多去搭 loop；token 焦虑这几周明显上来了；谁能把路由、重试、成本和效果一起压住，谁就更像下一层基础设施。

sections.headline: **Opus** for long autonomous runs: permissions, orchestration, and self-checks matter most · **Opus** 跑长时 автономous 任务，关键在权限、编排和自验证
sections.body:
Seeing a number of benchmarks showing Opus is the best model for long-running work.

Five tips for running Opus autonomously for hours/days:

1. Use auto mode for permissions, so Claude doesn’t ask for approval
2. Use dynamic workflows, to have Claude orchestrate hundreds/thousands of agents to get a task done
3. Use /goal or /loop, to nudge Claude to keep going until it’s done
4. Use Claude Code in the cloud, so you can close your laptop (easiest way is the desktop or mobile app)
5. Make sure Claude has a way to self-verify its work end to end: Claude in Chrome browser extension for web, iOS/Android sim MCP for mobile, a way to start the full web server or service for backend work

看到不少 benchmark 都在说明，**Opus** 现在最适合长时间连续工作。

如果想让 **Opus** 连跑几小时甚至几天，我的五个建议是：

1. 权限直接开 auto mode，这样 **Claude** 不会一直来找你批准
2. 用 dynamic workflows，让 **Claude** 编排几百到几千个 agent 一起把任务做完
3. 用 `/goal` 或 `/loop`，把 **Claude** 往前推，直到它把事情收尾
4. 把 **Claude Code** 放到云上跑，这样你可以直接合上电脑（最省事的是桌面或移动端 app）
5. 一定要给 **Claude** 一套端到端自验证的办法：网页场景用 **Claude** 的 **Chrome** 扩展，移动端用 iOS/Android 模拟器 MCP，后端场景要能把完整 web server 或服务真正拉起来

sections.headline: Frontier data work is high-skill labor, not grunt work · 前沿训练数据不是苦力活，而是高技能工种
sections.body:
A common misconception is that training data is low skill, grunt work - scan some notebooks, mine the internet, create labeled samples.

The data required to advance the model frontier is the opposite. Labs need training data for high-economic-value tasks. And most of these tasks outside of SWE have little documentation - it is complex, domain-specific knowledge built over the  years, spanning legacy tools that don’t talk to each other.

That's why we have SWE agents and not knowledge work agents yet.

The companies creating this training data, such as Mercor, are doing extremely high-leverage, high-skill work. 

Critical to moving AI forward. And deeply underappreciated.

一个常见误解是，训练数据是低技能的苦力活: 扫几本笔记、去网上扒资料、做些标注样本。

但真正推动模型前沿的数据，恰好相反。实验室需要的是高经济价值任务上的训练数据。而这些任务里，除了 SWE 之外，大多数都没多少现成文档可用，里面是多年积累下来的复杂领域知识，还牵扯一堆彼此不互通的老系统和工具。

这也是为什么我们先有了 SWE agent，却还没有真正成熟的知识工作 agent。

像 **Mercor** 这样做这类训练数据的公司，本质上干的是杠杆极高、门槛也很高的活。

这对推进 AI 很关键，但外界明显低估了。

sections.headline: Model families will split, and routing becomes the hard agent problem · 模型分层会更明显，路由会变成 agent 的硬骨头
sections.body:
The numbers may be a bit extreme here, but unquestionably use-cases have to stratify in the next year or two between model families.

We’ll see a split between frontier intelligence for high end tasks and work, and much cheaper models for high volume workloads that can sufficiently be peeled off to cheaper models. Frontier will still be far bigger than today because the use-cases will demand it, but the low-end will get quite a bit larger as well.

The big update here is that the layer that can efficiently route the workload to the right model will then become increasingly valuable since that becomes one of the new hard problems in AI agents. Agent orchestration that can cost optimize while still performing the task successfully will be in a strong position.

这里面的数字也许夸张了点，但可以肯定的是，未来一两年里，不同用例一定会在不同模型家族之间分层。

高端任务会继续吃前沿智能；高吞吐、大批量的工作，则会被尽可能剥离到更便宜的模型上。前沿模型的体量还是会比今天大得多，因为很多场景就得靠它；但低端模型那一层也会明显放大。

真正新的变化在于，能把工作高效路由到合适模型的那一层，会越来越值钱，因为这正在变成 AI agent 里最难的新问题之一。谁的 agent 编排既能压成本、又不把任务做砸，谁就会占住好位置。

sections.headline: AI makes software easier to build, but enterprise GTM stays brutally hard · AI 让软件更容易做了，但企业级 GTM 还是硬仗
sections.body:
This is what the market got wrong about AI eating enterprise software. Building good software in the past was very hard. Yes, AI has made that a bit easier, though it’s still hard to build something that’s got good taste, differentiated, high quality, secure, and so on.

But nevertheless, that’s only one component of building a platform that enterprises rely on. The plurality of costs in most enterprise software companies is actually on GTM, because at scale most enterprise software categories are tough to break into and need a heavy amount of consultative selling and support for implementation and integration of solutions.  

AI hasn’t reduced the need for that, and in many cases requires it even more now, as landscapes get even more busy and complicated for buyers to navigate through. If you make one thing cheaper and more abundant (development of software) then the new problem of discoverability and market differentiation (GTM) becomes the hardest part.

市场对“AI 会吃掉企业软件”这件事，理解偏了。过去做出好软件确实很难。没错，AI 让这件事轻松了一点，但要做出有品位、有差异化、高质量、够安全的产品，依然不容易。

但这也只是企业平台建设的一部分。多数企业软件公司的大头成本，其实花在 GTM 上，因为一旦做到规模，很多企业软件赛道都很难切进去，必须靠很重的顾问式销售，以及实施、集成上的支持。

AI 并没有让这部分需求消失，很多时候反而更需要，因为买方面对的选择越来越乱、越来越复杂。你把一件事变便宜、变充足了（软件开发），那新的难题就会变成可发现性和市场差异化，也就是 GTM。

sections.headline: IPO liquidity doesn’t just buy leisure; it restarts the **Silicon Valley** loop · IPO 带来的流动性不只换来躺平，也会把 **硅谷** 的循环再点起来
sections.body:
I have had the chance to go through two IPOs (Meta and Dropbox).

Fabulous wealth tends to amplify deeper desires, not create new ones.

The mainstream narrative is: "Early Employees make lots of money and buy mansions and go to the beach".

For some: Yes, they want to chill. That is great. I am happy for them.

But for a lot of folks, it is a chance to do even crazier and wackier stuff. Start new things. Fund new things. Keep the crazy loop of Silicon Valley going.

It's going to be awesome to have a lot of folks with liquidity in the coming months. 

Onwards!.

我亲历过两次 IPO（**Meta** 和 **Dropbox**）。

巨额财富通常不是平白造出新的欲望，而是把人心里本来更深的那些东西放大。

主流叙事总爱说：“早期员工赚了很多钱，然后去买豪宅、去海边躺着。”

有些人确实会这样。挺好，我也替他们高兴。

但对很多人来说，这反而是一个机会，去做更疯、更野的事。再创点新东西。再投点新东西。把 **Silicon Valley** 那个疯狂循环继续滚下去。

接下来几个月，会有很多人手上开始有流动性，这会很有意思。

继续往前。

items.person_name: The MAD Podcast with Matt Turck

sections.headline: **Aaron Levie** on enterprise AI: model progress is outrunning deployment, and token cost is now a boardroom problem · **Aaron Levie** 谈企业 AI：模型跑太快，落地跟不上，token 成本已经进了会议室
sections.body:
**Matt Turck** talks with **Box CEO Aaron Levie** about the strange state of enterprise AI in 2026: coding agents have already hit escape velocity inside engineering teams, but the rest of the enterprise is still stuck moving from chatbots to real agents. Levie’s core point is blunt: breakthroughs keep landing faster than customers can standardize on an architecture, so each new jump in capability can make the last rollout feel outdated before it finishes.

He says the mood among CIOs is still more optimistic than cynical because they can already see real gains from tools like **Codex**, **Cursor**, and cloud coding systems inside IT. But that optimism is colliding with hard operational questions: token budgets, deployment talent, workflow design, and the challenge of turning agent demos into durable business processes. His framing of “tokenmaxxing” versus enterprise budget planning stands out as one of the episode’s sharpest tensions.

**Matt Turck** 跟 **Box** CEO **Aaron Levie** 聊的是 2026 年企业 AI 最别扭的现实：工程团队里的 coding agent 已经跑出速度了，非工程部门却还卡在“从聊天机器人过渡到真 agent”这一步。Levie 讲得很直接，模型突破来得比客户定架构还快，所以你刚把上一轮 rollout 做到一半，下一轮能力升级又把它搞得像旧方案。

他判断 CIO 的整体情绪其实没外界想得那么悲观，因为他们已经在 IT 部门里看到了 **Codex**、**Cursor** 和云端 coding 工具带来的实打实效率提升。但乐观归乐观，真正难的都在后面：token 预算怎么管、有没有人能把系统部署起来、workflow 怎么设计、agent demo 怎么变成能长期跑的业务流程。节目里最有力的一条线索，就是“tokenmaxxing”和企业预算纪律之间那股越来越拧巴的张力。

sections.headline: **Claude Managed Agents** adds dreaming, outcomes, and multiagent orchestration · **Claude Managed Agents** 新增 dreaming、结果评分和多 agent 编排
sections.body:
**Anthropic** is expanding **Claude Managed Agents** with three notable capabilities. “Dreaming,” launched as a research preview, reviews past sessions and memory stores to extract patterns and improve future behavior. “Outcomes” adds a separate grader loop so agents can evaluate their work against a rubric and revise before returning results. Multiagent orchestration lets a lead agent split work across specialists that run in parallel on a shared filesystem.

The post leans hard on practical gains rather than abstract agent rhetoric. **Anthropic** says outcomes improved task success by up to 10 points in testing, with especially strong results on harder tasks and file generation like **docx** and **pptx**. It also highlights customer examples from **Harvey**, **Netflix**, **Every**, and **Wisedocs**, all pointing in the same direction: agents are being pushed toward longer-running, self-checking, and more distributed workflows.

**Anthropic** 这篇更新，给 **Claude Managed Agents** 补了三块很关键的能力。第一块是 research preview 里的“dreaming”，它会回看过去的会话和记忆库，抽模式、修记忆，让 agent 下一次少踩坑。第二块是“outcomes”，相当于多了一层独立评分回路，agent 会照着 rubric 自查，不达标就再改。第三块是多 agent 编排，让一个主 agent 把任务拆给不同 specialist，在共享文件系统上并行干活。

这篇文章可取的地方是没空谈什么 agent 愿景，而是直接报实际收益。**Anthropic** 说，outcomes 在测试里最多把任务成功率拉高了 10 个点，难任务和 **docx**、**pptx** 这类文件生成尤其明显。文里举的 **Harvey**、**Netflix**、**Every**、**Wisedocs** 也都指向同一件事：agent 正在从“会聊两句”往“能长时间跑、会自己复查、还能分工协作”那边走。
